rule_level_problems.problem: Every red-box item is at Urgent, but VHA's warning_signs already carry higher levels for several of them: 'Burn of face' and inhalation burn are Emergency, 'Chemical burn', circumferential burn and 'Burn Over 20%' are Very urgent. The briefing says to use the level the corresponding warning sign already carries. The page's own wording ('urgent attention') justifies Urgent, so this is a house-standard mismatch rather than a page error, but the rule will under-prioritise relative to the warning-signs page.

The footnote defining shock ('shock likely' if SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) is not encoded as a probable Shock rule; the priority rule only fires on shock if the nurse records 'Shock' directly or SBP < 80. Pulse >= 100, RR > 30, restlessness and weakness never contribute.

Both possible rules fire on 'Cigarette burn' only; the page's other three triggers (burn with a specific shape, repeated/unexplained burns, other unexplained injuries) are dropped without any approximation such as 'Non-accidental injury' (disorder), which exists in SNOMED.

Circumferential burn is encoded as three site-specific forms (chest wall / upper limb / lower limb + Circumferential). VHA's 'Burn Circumferential' warning sign records the general form (Burn + Circumferential), which is not a descendant of any of the three, so a burn recorded through the warning-signs page will not satisfy this rule. Using (Burn + Circumferential) would match both the general record and the site-specific ones.

Inhalation injury is only accepted as (active_condition ...). VHA's 'Burn Inhalation' warning sign records (clinical_finding 'Inhalation burn due to hot gas'), which this rule ignores; adding that clinical_finding (or the parent) to the or-list would close the gap. Low because the warning sign already carries Emergency on its own.

'Cigarette burn' sits in the 'Check for urgent burn features' task although it is a non-urgent-pathway finding; cosmetic, but the task description misleads. 'Over 70 percent body burnt' in the TBSA list is redundant with the 70-79/80-89/90+ bands, and the 10-19 band admits exactly 10% where the page says > 10%.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully: all twelve criteria, including the inhalation-injury 'likely' as a probable rule consumed by the priority rule and 'other injury' as Traumatic injury excluding Burn, check out concept by concept. The main gaps are outside the box: the footnote that defines shock ('shock likely' from SBP, pulse, RR, confusion, weakness) has no probable rule, and the abuse/self-harm 'consider' rules fire on cigarette burns only, dropping the page's other three triggers. The whole rule sits at Urgent although VHA's warning signs already carry Emergency/Very urgent for facial, inhalation, chemical, circumferential and >20% burns.
